page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.24xlarge is a general-purpose, compute-dense cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R05 processor featuring 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a 5.0 GHz clock speed, with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and contains no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage. Hardware acceleration is limited to CPU-native instruction sets, including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic extensions, with no discrete GPUs attached.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for raw computational throughput and system concurrency. In stress-ng evaluations, it achieved 4,209.07 in single-core and 400,627.90 in multi-core metrics. Geekbench scoring registered 3,111 for single-core and 31,298 for multi-core workloads, supported by high throughput across Clang compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory subsystem testing demonstrated an uncached read bandwidth of 1,055.41 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 398.63 GB/sec, which underpins strong performance in in-memory operations such as Redis SET handling at 332.74 million operations per second.

Resource allocation provides high operational efficiency for large-scale enterprise deployments requiring massive parallel processing alongside high network throughput. The lack of simultaneous multithreading means each vCPU corresponds to a full dedicated core, preventing noisy-neighbor contention inside the guest and delivering predictable single-thread execution. However, the total absence of integrated local ephemeral storage shifts IOPS dependence entirely onto networked EBS volumes, which represents an architectural consideration for disk-intensive workflows.

Given its combination of high clock speed, 96 dedicated physical cores, 384.0 GB DDR5 memory, and 200 Gbps networking, the instance is suited for multi-threaded distributed compilation, large-scale Redis or in-memory key-value caching, network-bound web serving fleets, enterprise databases, and CPU-based machine learning prompt tokenization.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor with 96 dedicated physical cores (96 vCPUs) clocked at 5.0 GHz. It features 384.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no integrated local storage and no discrete GPUs, utilizing network EBS for persistence. Benchmark performance ranks in the top decile across multi-core compute, compiler workloads, and memory throughput, executing 332.74 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining 1,055.41 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. With dedicated execution threads and vector instruction sets including AVX-512, this instance is suited for large-scale distributed caching, CI/CD compilation pipelines, enterprise backend services, and network-intensive data processing.
